15.0.0.en: As a result of the people's persistence in their sins, God forbids Jeremiah to pray for them; and lest he think it is because of his own weakness or sins, He says to him that not even the great prophets among God's people, such as Moses, who interceded for his people lest God destroy them (Ex 32:11-14), and such as Samuel (1 Sam 7:5-11), could help. This is an encouragement to Jeremiah, of whom the Holy Bible records that he is a constant intercessor for the children of God (2 Macc 15). And God decides that He must cast His people away and drive them out of their cities as a discipline for their sins, that perhaps they may repent.

15.0.1.en: Beware of losing the intercession of the saints for you through your persistence in sin and your justifying it, so that your guardian angel grieves over you. Whatever your faults, do not despair or grieve, but offer repentance before your father of confession, and God will receive you.

15.1.0.en: God says to Jeremiah: If they ask you, “Where shall we go when we go out from our cities?” you will declare to them God's decree, which appears in:

15.1.1.en: 1- Death by the sword and by every means.

15.1.2.en: 2- Sickness because of hunger, which may lead to death.

15.1.3.en: 3- Captivity as slaves in the kingdom of Babylon.

15.2.0.en: God affirms His severe punishment of them because of their persistence in sin, and this punishment appears in:

15.2.1.en: 1- Death by the sword, which means their destruction because of their lack of repentance.

15.2.2.en: 2- The dogs dragging their corpses after their death, a symbol of their humiliation because of their sins.

15.2.3.en: 3- The birds of prey eating their corpses, a symbol of the demons who attack them with evil thoughts and pagan worship.

15.2.4.en: 4- The beasts eating their corpses, a symbol of the evil desires that destroy their lives.

15.3.0.en: In addition to the previous punishments, God strikes them with anxiety when Babylon takes them captive and carries them to scattered lands in its kingdom. All this is because of their persistence in the evils in which King Manasseh excelled, who was the most wicked of the kings of the kingdom of Judah and reigned for a long time, and introduced the worship of idols into his kingdom, and depravity spread in his days; so the Jews continued in these sins in the days of Jeremiah.

15.4.0.en: Jerusalem will be in a state of great misery after Babylon destroys her, and she will find none among her neighbors to have pity on her and help her, nor among the cities of Judah, because they will have been destroyed like her; and God will not rescue her because she rebelled against Him and disobeyed His word.

15.5.0.en: Because Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah forsook God and life with Him and replaced Him with the worship of idols, God allows this punishment to come upon her, and God declares His weariness with her false repentance, for she is not sincere in her worship and pretends repentance and regret, while persisting in evil.

15.6.0.en: Fan: a wooden stick with five fingers used to separate the grain from the chaff, so that the chaff flies away with the wind, far from the grain.

15.6.1.en: The gates of the land: the whole world.

15.6.2.en: I will bereave: I will kill the sons of My people.

15.6.3.en: God threatens His people that He will scatter them in the cities of the world by means of Babylon, which reigns over the world and carries them to various lands subject to it; and He likens this to the farmer who winnows the chaff to remove it and separate it from the grains of wheat or barley. He adds also that He will kill the sons of the kingdom of Judah, so that she becomes like the bereaved mother, that is, one who has lost her children.

15.7.0.en: Terrors: the plural of “terror,” something very frightening. God declares that He will kill many of the men of Judah, so that the number of widows increases to the point that it becomes difficult to count them, as it is impossible to count the sand of the seas; and death will fall suddenly upon the mother who has young sons and kill her sons, causing her great terror and fear. This is what happened at the hand of Babylon, which killed the young men and left their mothers without sons.

15.8.0.en: He continues His speech about the mothers of the kingdom of Judah who lost their young sons in the war, and likens her to a woman who in her weakness has become like a languishing woman because she lost all her sons, even if they were many and reached seven sons; that is, the Jewish nation lost all her men and surrendered to sorrow and fell into an affliction expressed by darkness, though she is not old, but she lost her vitality as the day loses its light and the night comes with its darkness. And she was in shame, disgrace, humiliation and weakness because of the death of the men who were her support. So she is a type of the soul that grew careless and persisted in sin and so became helpless and unable to face life. All this God says through Jeremiah to warn His people, that they may return from their depravity, desires and pagan worship, and repent, and God will receive them.

15.9.0.en: Jeremiah began to prophesy when he was young, in the midst of a wicked generation, and he rebuked the people to repent, and likewise their leaders, whether priests or prophets or rulers; and only a very small number accepted his word and repented, among them his disciple the prophet Baruch, who recorded the prophecies of his teacher. As for the rest of the people, they felt distress at Jeremiah's words, indeed they considered him an agent of Babylon when he called them to submit to the Babylonian captivity and not to take refuge in Egypt; so they stood as adversaries to him and resisted him and contended with him, and even tried many times to kill him. Yet there were no material dealings between him and them: he had not lent to them, nor borrowed anything from them, for these material dealings are what cause disputes among men; he demanded no debt and no one demanded debts from him, but everyone cursed him because he rebuked them and spoke to them about the future, which was an injustice to them and not good news like the false prophets; and his contention was with all the inhabitants of the land of the kingdom of Judah, that is, all his people.

15.9.1.en: This verse shows Jeremiah's distress at the people's resistance to his prophecies, so that he calls to his mother according to the flesh. He is in pain and the closest person to him is his mother, to whom he declares the extent of his inner pain because of his service to them.

15.9.2.en: Do not give up proclaiming the truth as long as God has guided you to it, even if people reject your word, and bear their abuses, because they resist you in ignorance, and pray for them.

15.10.0.en: God answers Jeremiah, who is suffering from his people's abuses toward him, and promises him that He will free him from the chains of the prison into which he was thrown and from the chains of the inner pains that he suffers because of his people's persecution of him.

15.10.1.en: Then He reassures him, because he said to himself: If my own people persecute me like this, what will the Babylonian enemies do to me? And God answers him that He will make the enemies treat him well, indeed that they will entreat him to do what he wishes. This is what actually happened, for the Babylonians honored him and left him free to stay in Jerusalem or go to Babylon. And what is meant by the time of evil and affliction is the time of Babylon's attack on the kingdom of Judah.

15.11.0.en: The LORD speaks to His people by the mouth of Jeremiah and says to him: If you think that you are strong like iron, can you break the iron and the brass that come from the north, that is, the kingdom of Babylon? Of course not; rather Babylon will defeat you and destroy you.

15.12.0.en: Thy borders: your boundaries. God continues His speech to His people, who will be defeated before Babylon, and says to them that Babylon will plunder all your wealth and everything in your treasures of gold or silver or precious possessions, and will occupy your land to all your borders, because you have sinned greatly against God. So the enemy takes all your possessions without price, not in exchange for anything but because of your sins.

15.13.0.en: And after Babylon plunders all the possessions of the kingdom of Judah, it will seize the rich, the great men and the young men, and send them as slaves to Babylon and all the cities of its kingdom, because on account of their sins the fire of God's anger was kindled against it.

15.13.1.en: Be humble and rely on God, and do not rely on your own strength in resisting whoever wrongs you; all your wealth, relationships and position will not profit you if you do not keep God's commandments. So return to Him in repentance and trust in Him, and He will keep you from all evil.

15.14.0.en: When the afflictions, insults and threats from the wicked against Jeremiah increased, he pleaded with God, saying:

15.14.1.en: 1- You alone, O God, know the secrets of my heart, and that I love You and love my people and want their salvation. So if the wicked think me a traitor in my own country or harsh toward them, You know that I do all this for their good.

15.14.2.en: 2- He asks God not to forget him and leave him alone in the midst of the persecutors, but to care for him and look after him with His mercies and deliver him from their hands.

15.14.3.en: 3- Jeremiah was weary of the persecution of the false prophets against him, so that he asked God to take vengeance on them, not out of spite and hatred for them but to discipline them, so that they stop their false teachings and repent and no longer wrong him.

15.14.4.en: 4- If Jeremiah declared his distress to his mother over the troubles he was going through, in (v. 10), this does not mean that he wants to die, but he wants to complete his mission and prophesy as God commands him to draw his people to repentance; so he asks God to be longsuffering toward him and not let him die because he declared his pains and his distress at the persecutions, but to support him and give him an opportunity to complete his service.

15.14.5.en: 5- Jeremiah reminded God that he had borne many insults for His sake, so that God would make an excuse for him in his distress at the multitude of pains, and support and strengthen him.

15.15.0.en: In the midst of all these pains God comforted Jeremiah by letting him taste the sweetness of God's word, and the prophet declares this by saying that God's word is very delightful, so that he hid it in his heart and meditated on it, and it became a great source of joy to him in the midst of pains; and he expresses the depth of his meditation by saying that he ate God's word. He adds that this grace was given to him, namely delighting in God's word, because God's name is called upon him, that is, God gave him the grace of prophecy and brought him into the depths of His word, which is the greatest wealth in the world, while the wealth of his people who persist in evil becomes worthless and is plundered by Babylon; but as for God's word, no one can take it away from Jeremiah, because it is the word of the LORD God of hosts, that is, the mighty God, able to establish His word in His children and protect them by it.

15.15.1.en: Do not be content with reading the Holy Bible every day, but take care to meditate on its meanings, and choose a verse to memorize and make it an exercise that you apply in your life.

15.16.0.en: Jeremiah lived in godliness and rejected the councils of the mockers and their vain talk, and sat alone meditating on the word of God and grieving over his people who were far away and over their evil future, that is, their captivity; and his heart was filled with distress, sorrow and anger because of their persistence in evil, and he prayed to deliver them from it.

15.17.0.en: Jeremiah asks in his distress from the pains and rebukes God, who leaves him with a wounded heart and inner pains because of his people's lack of repentance, in addition to the constant insults and persecutions against him, and he says to Him: Your leaving me is as if You were a false god, who promises His children to rescue them from affliction yet leaves me to pains. Then he rebukes God, likening Him to a spring of water that is not lasting, so that a man comes to it and finds no water, that is, no comfort. Here Jeremiah rebukes God, asking for His quick intervention to rescue him from those who persecute him.

15.18.0.en: God makes an excuse for Jeremiah in his suffering and his not enduring the persecutions, but He calls him to return to his steadfast faith in Him; then God will restore to him his peace and tranquility, for He appreciates his human weakness but promises him peace and joy if he returns to his reliance on Him. What is meant by Jeremiah's standing before God is the standing of prayer and the feeling of God's constant presence with him, so that his heart is reassured, and then he can speak with courage and declare his prophecies however much the wicked persecute him. And bringing forth the precious from the vile, that is, the good, fat meat from the bones or membranes that are not eaten, means bringing back to God the precious souls that were despised because of their evil. So God encourages the prophet to be strong and complete his service of seeking the repentance of the souls of his people; by this his mouth will be as God's mouth, that is, he declares the divine truth and shows the fatherhood of God, who desires the salvation of all. And by this the people will return to the pure life that Jeremiah lives in faith and leave the worship of idols, and Jeremiah will not return to rebuke them again for their evils.

15.18.1.en: It may be that what is meant by Jeremiah's not returning to them is that he will not rebuke them again, because the captivity will fall upon them and they will return to Jeremiah asking him to rescue them.

15.19.0.en: God reassures Jeremiah that although his people persecute him, He will support him and make him strong like the brazen walls that surround cities, which no one can break through; they will continue their persecutions but will not be able to stop his prophecies or weaken him.

15.20.0.en: Thus the power of God is manifested: although the wicked who persecute Jeremiah are strong, and he describes them as terrible, that is, very strong, God rescues him from their hands, and God's power, which is above all, is revealed.

15.20.1.en: Return to God in repentance and hold to your faith, and you will receive divine power that supports you, so that no one can overcome you and you are able to continue in the life of purity and the service of God.

15.20.2.en: Jeremiah's life as an example for the people

16.0.0.en: God commanded Jeremiah not to marry and therefore not to beget sons and daughters, because the captivity had drawn near and many would be killed and the rest taken as captives, so that Jeremiah would not be exposed to anxiety because his wife and children were killed or taken as slaves far from him, and so that he might be an example to the people and a declaration of the nearness of the captivity when they ask him the reason for his not marrying, that they may believe the truth of what he says and repent of their evils that cause this captivity.

16.1.0.en: Dung: the waste of man and beast. Lamented: the sad words of lament that are said in the mourning for the dead.

16.1.1.en: He declares the reason for Jeremiah's not marrying, which is a prophecy that the mothers, daughters and sons of God's people will die by the sword of Babylon or sicken from hunger, and more than this, that no mourning or lament will be made for them and that no one will bury their corpses, but they will be thrown on the face of the ground as dung or eaten by the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, as a declaration of the humiliation that will befall them at the hand of the Babylonians.

16.2.0.en: God forbade Jeremiah to attend funerals or the mourning made when a person dies, so that if they ask him he may declare to them what will happen at the captivity, where no mourning will be made at anyone's death, but the corpses will be thrown on the ground and the rest will flee. All this is because God will withhold His peace, kindness and care from His people, that perhaps they may repent.

16.3.0.en: Cut themselves: wound themselves at the death of their loved ones to please the pagan gods.

16.3.1.en: Baldness: the nearest of kin to the dead used to shave the hair of his head and beard to please the pagan gods. He affirms that when Babylon attacks, great and small will be killed and the rest will flee, and there will be no opportunity to perform the rites of mourning such as lament, cutting the bodies and shaving the hair to please the pagan gods whom they worshiped, and because the bodies will not be buried at all but will remain thrown on the ground.

16.4.0.en: In ancient times the comforters did as some do now: they bring food and drink to the house of the dead to share with his family in the funeral meal, but this will not be, for no funerals will be held and the corpses will not even be buried when Babylon attacks. In sum, when Jeremiah does not attend the mournings, he declares to the people that the reason is God's warning to them of the captivity coming upon them, that they may repent.

16.5.0.en: Likewise God forbade Jeremiah to attend feasts of joy or to share in the food and drink offered in them.

16.6.0.en: The reason for not attending feasts of joy is that God will bring them to an end when the captivity comes, so that all will be in sorrow and will not hold the feasts of joy that are held after the completion of a marriage or on other occasions.

16.6.1.en: Look at the lives of the saints to learn from them how to live with God and prepare for your eternity, and then you will not be wearied by the wars of the devil, since you will be strong in God like these saints.

16.7.s.en: (2) Sin is the cause of the captivity

16.7.0.en: The LORD declares to Jeremiah that when he prophesies to them of the captivity coming upon them as a discipline, they will be astonished, because they do not commit sins that deserve this, and they will ask, “What is our sin?” This shows the spiritual blindness that came upon the people because of their immersion in sin and the breaking of their relationship with God, so that they fell into great ignorance and lack of discernment.

16.8.0.en: The LORD asked Jeremiah to answer them that the causes are:

16.8.1.en: 1- The worship of idols and the evils that their fathers did and their forsaking God, so the sons were influenced and learned these sins from their fathers.

16.8.2.en: 2- Their continuing in the sins of their fathers, indeed their increasing in them.

16.8.3.en: 3- Their rejecting the voice of God through the mouth of Jeremiah and their stubbornness against him.

16.8.4.en: 4- When the Babylonians drive them out of their land and carry them to the lands of their kingdom, they will continue in the worship of idols to which they were accustomed, not only by day for fear of the enemies but also by night, because they loved this worship, so they offer it from their hearts out of conviction; and the grace of God will depart from them, and they will suffer material and spiritual wrong because of their persistence in sin.

16.8.5.en: If you see faults in your parents or in any person, do not judge him, but try to avoid these sins and acquire the opposite virtues, so that you do a positive work and save your soul by the power of Christ.

16.9.s.en: (3) Sin is the cause of the captivity

16.9.3.en: God declares that He will discipline His people by sending the Babylonians against them as fishers and hunters, who will catch them and kill them even if they hide in the mountains and hills or the clefts of the rocks; that is, they must perish because of their sins.

16.10.0.en: God is longsuffering, but He sees all the sins of His people, even if they commit them in secret, and in the end He must punish them for them. But even in disciplining them He asks that they repent, so He warns them of His discipline that they may repent, for He is a tender Father who does not desire the destruction of His people.

16.11.0.en: The carcases of their detestable things: the animals slaughtered to the pagan gods.

16.11.1.en: As a result of God's people's immersion in the worship of idols and their rejection of God, He will punish them with a severe, double punishment fitting their great evil, their provoking God and their defiling the Promised Land with the worship of idols.

16.12.0.en: My strength: my glory and my pride.

16.12.1.en: The prophet speaks to God in the midst of the afflictions that he meets from his people who are far from God, and trusts in the LORD, his fortress and refuge in afflictions, indeed his glory and his pride. And he prophesies about the Gentiles' faith in Christ, who will declare that their worship of idols is a lie and that the true God is Christ.

16.13.0.en: Then the prophet declares that God will make the Gentiles know His name and His might, so that they believe in Him and leave the pagan gods, and know that He is Jehovah, that is, He is God and there is no other.

16.13.1.en: Do not be troubled by the resistance of the wicked, for they are weak and will submit to your Christ in the end and will feel His power that is in you; so abide in your faith and pray for them.

16.13.2.en: Reliance on God, our Savior from sin
